summary:
# NOTES (two books)

## BOOK 1: "In Sargasso." MISSING, A ROMANCE
Author: Julius Chambers. Pub. 1896, Transatlantic Publishing Co., NY/London. Narrator: Capt. Austin Clark.

**Preface:** Sargasso Sea within a week's sail of NY. Seaweed, orchids, vines. Lost ships end there ("Harbor of Missing Ships"). Signed J.C.

**Ch I (Knight-Errant):** Clark, American, born/raised Brooklyn. Apprenticed on Black Ball line (NY–Liverpool). Cameron & Co., age 23 2nd mate on Australian ship; 4 voyages round Horn to Melbourne; 1st mate; at 27 commanded 3 months after captain's accident. Offered captaincy of tramp steamer *Caribas* (named for Marquis of that name), sent from Plymouth by Triplett & Jones; lying Erie Basin NY. Crew 40; posted "Missing" at Lloyds NY & London. Tramp commander = "commercial knight-errant."

**Ch II (Fatal Curiosity):** Sailed Harbeck's Stores, NY, fair June day, for Azores (Horta, Ponte Delgada, then Lisbon). Passenger **Arthur Gray**, claims artist; carries a **Secor launch** (direct-explosion engine, extra shear). Three days out, at Gray's urging, Clark turned SE after longitude 40. Day 5: derelicts. Gazetteer: Sargasso 22–28°N, 25–60°W, ~200,000 sq mi (≈Texas). Argonauts reference ("islands clapped together"). Clark anchored/made fast to water-logged full-rigged ship listing 25°. Dawn mirage in eastern sky: ships separated by sod strips, "City of Ships." Masthead lookout reports moving objects. Clark resolves to explore. Takes quadrant, one chronometer, days' provisions. First mate left in charge; 2nd mate asked to come, refused with frown/headshake. Launch hoisted by derrick from foremast. Left ~9 AM, Clark at tiller. Canal width ≈ Grand Canal, Venice.

**Ch III (Betrayed):** Gray took the repeating rifle "to shoot wild fowl," kept it forward. Gray knows channel landmarks (redwood tree, logwood trunk, wire grass, sunken tree). Engine quit (Gray's false adjustment); oars dropped overboard unseen. Clark's revolver contained no loaded cartridges; he dropped his cartridge belt into the sea. Gray: "They are my countrymen!" Hailed by ships in many languages; Clark speaks Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Norwegian, Russian, German, Greek, Danish. Landed on floating sod (serpents, insects; marmosets once existed, exterminated). Ladder up the hulk (~25 ft out of water). **Kantoon** of that family: ~60, grizzled gray beard trimmed 3 inches, porpoise-skin dress, dark-brown leather cap, stands in tub of water. Gray introduces Clark as "fine boat...accession." Clark locked in small room, bolt outside; carved/burned pictures on walls (like Tower of London cells).

**Ch IV (People of the Sea):** Gray in shark-skin knee breeches and laced jacket, barefoot. Gray: "We must grow." Chief Kantoon will make Clark master of own ship after destroying engines/propeller. Gray's story: schooner from Bermuda to Canaries; captain set him adrift with smallpox; picked up by Sargassons; 5 years among them. Crew "taken alive" must navigate ship to the area, then join or receive "the mercy of extinction." Gray allowed to visit US, swore oath; "I am a Sargasson." Gray's words: "Grand Kantoon—who rules the sea, and the air." Night: no lights; Clark dreams of death.

**Ch V (Manners and Customs):** Breakfast: thick brown drink from parasitic plant (exhilarating), two biscuits from launch stores (Sargassons scrupulously honest). Gray opens cell; warns that murder = drowning in barrel by six men. Audience with Kantoon, who speaks polyglot ("Morning, Senor Captaine. Es usted very good, aujourd'hui? Sitzen sie down." / "Io sono the Kantoon de cette ship." / "Quel difference? Sit upon the deck."). Clark recalls Salvini's Italian Hamlet. Kantoon's history: origin 300+ yrs ago, Spanish Armada galleons caught in Central Atlantic whirlpool; early 1800s African slave ship mutinied, joined; Portuguese/Spanish intermarriage; wars over the Sacred Light; ships last ~50 years; death chant when ship sinks; disobedient children lashed to ship and starved or sharked. Clark rants against explorers (Cook, Magellan, Franklin, Drake). Clark overhears plot (Spanish & French speakers) to take Caribas that night. Locked in; heavy mist.

**Ch VI (Attack on the Caribas):** Red light in sky = **Sacred Fire**: locomotive headlight (salvaged 20 yrs earlier, magnifying lens) over embers on iron cook-hulk; reflection on cloud. Priest of Sacred Fire gives life as bond. Boats: grass matting, fish-scale gum, paddles strung with fish-gut thongs; ~9 ft; carry 2. Kantoon narrates attack plan: 200 men; red-pepper/Tabasco-like dust in fish bladders plus opium-like fungus drug (sape-like). Only firearm: Clark's Winchester (~6 cartridges left). Gray's boat had three people; two men had orders to lasso/capsize him if treacherous. 50 miles in ~8 hrs. Boats hid in two parks; canoe boys handle painters. Caribas moored to dismasted hulk (listed 25°). Signal = ship's bell.

**Ch VII (Agony of Suspense):** Kantoon narrates: boatswain (sturdy, veteran) saw Sacred Light, suspected trouble, skipped "eight bells," woke next watch; mates ignored him. Boatswain's whistle roused crew; defensive party of ~12 with cloths over faces; dust repelled. Cabin boy begged for life; killed; dropped with weight. Crew mostly knocked out with marlin spikes and tossed overboard. Boatswain, tied to davit, chopped cables while fighting. Asked that cabin boy be spared (unaware he was dead). Chose drowning in water butt (cask head knocked out, filled in 3 minutes); six men held him; Kantoon shook his hand and turned away. Ship's engines re-steamed by morning. Kantoon gives Clark his own binoculars. Clark sees smoke from Caribas, ~6 miles away. Clark despairs. Thieving unknown in Sargasso.

**Ch VIII (Fidette):** Young woman's voice awakens him. **Fidette**: small, perfect figure, hazel-brown eyes, reddish-brown hair, pearly teeth. Blue-and-gray sea-grass mantle clasped with shark teeth; shell-studded leather girdle; bare feet. Holds sprig of rhododendron (Sargasson emblem of tender affection) and wicker tray of wintergreen-like berries. Speaks Creole French. Five days' isolation for captives. Her mother: New Orleans, daughter of a "place woman," convent-schooled, eloped with gambler son of a sugar planter (planter's father a brigadier-general). Summer 1872 Saratoga trip by steamer; leak; mother hid in bunk; ship deserted. Steamer identified as *George Cornwall*, Capt. Timothy Rogers, lost from New Orleans. Mother alone ~5 months; drifted into Sargasso. Kantoon (captor) chose her as his prize; Deputy Chief Kantoon married them; gifts of jewels; Kantoon shaved and wore sea-grass cravat. Clark kisses Fidette.

**Ch IX (An Old Man's Darling):** Kantoon angry (cabin boy saw kiss). Threatens Clark: Clark to be executive on sinking ship; Fidette never to see him again; Caribas to be Kantoon's cantonment. Clark takes blame. Kantoon: Fidette had hysteria; "I am a fool." Kantoon: mother the prettiest woman; mother taught Fidette French; Kantoon cannot read. Mother died 6 months earlier of fever. Ship had 85 people. Kantoon sole allowed a wife; Kantoon's authority; first mate handles dry rot and moistening. Abandoned barnacle-laden bark: Kantoon forbids relief. Heaven: level country, 3 ft warm water. Diet: seaweed farina, sun-dried fish; Ogalla berries. Wife of Kantoon executed for abuse. Death sentence: hands and feet bound into a "D," kissed, dirge, tossed by two most-loved.

**Ch X (Cooking for All):** Clark guards Fidette's morning swim with spear-pole from board. Floating kitchen (cook-ship), condensers unused; water from shellacked awning. Requisition on tarpon scale. Caribas moored in new slip; Clark sees her crew. Barnacle chowder. Return greeted by Fidette's voice.

**Ch XI (Music Hath Charms):** Bowsprit with feet in water. Fidette's prior love: **Don Fernandez Otranto**, son of exiled Portuguese marshal, escaped from Azores penal servitude, father died of thirst. Fernandez adopted by Kantoon of the Royal George (ex-Sir John Franklin ship). Sprig of bay exchanged. Fernandez played trombone (educated Paris, Heidelberg). Homely hunchback daughter of Kantoon of Green Octopod (Royal George renamed) jealous; corrupted an officer; Green Octopod sank with Fernandez aboard (per Fidette). Then trombone heard at night. Fidette's face: joy. Fernandez alive.

**Ch XII (Jealous Heart):** Clark jealous. Ship absent from horizon. Fidette cold: "Week of Silence" festival; will dance Bamboola with Fernandez after.

**Ch XIII (Week of Silence):** Sun-Glorification dance at 3 AM. Week-long sleep; Bantang (Day of Awakening). "Dance of the Derelicts" with Fidette hornpipe; Kantoon and chief mate. Clark rations food into seven portions. Trombone again. Fidette at window.

**Ch XIV (Kantoon's Displeasure):** Visiting day. Fernandez visits without customary bluefish scale; Fidette douses him with bucket. Fernandez put in sack and drowned by the Kantoon. Clark glad. Fidette laughs on bowsprit.

**Ch XV (Chin-Goone Revolt):** Clark formally accepted as son-in-law. Month of "Visitation": women visitors, gossip, dress (sea-grass, no sewing), shark-bone hairpins, Greek girls with silk and sprig of sea myrtle, octopus pets; sea-water bucket baptism; women over 200 lbs drowned. Gossip vilifies Fidette (vampire). Kantoon barrels talk (both in tubs). Chin-Goone rebellion 1816 (200 Kantoons plot to rescue Napoleon from St. Helena); Chin-Goone scuttled 100 ships with ship's auger; executed one year later. Portuguese crew rebels; plans to abduct Fidette. Clark recalls *Wabash* Virginius-era night watch.

**Ch XVI (Papier-Maché Oranges):** Orange-hued spheres in hanging basket = detonating fireworks made in Wilmington, Del. Clark recalls Brandywine Creek factory explosion (dead women and men; crates of shells). Kantoon used them for ink. Clark warns: radius 25 ft. Fidette: "blood oranges." Rebel leader **Hansko Yap**, son of distinguished Kantoon, short half-inch of required six feet; sentenced to die; led 50 rebels; seized derelict; 80-ft capped spar (foremast) as battering ram; swimmers take it under arm; sank a dozen ships.

**Ch XVII (Spar Fight):** Clark's morning watch; spar approaches; Sargasson swimmers belly-up sharks technique (double-edged knives). Kantoon hands Clark a sword. Boats attacked; swimmers dive under boats, rip bottoms; ~all boat crew killed. Kantoon, cutlass in hand, kills two; hamstrung by a Lascar and killed. Clark uses rope fender to stop spar twice; 29 heads, then ~18 (11 lost). Boarders reach hatch; Fidette's act.

**Ch XVIII (Fruit for Dead Men):** Quarter never asked. Hatch covered (protecting wounded). Six men on quarterdeck. Fidette: "I must die"-type farewell; playful lock of Clark's hair. She climbs rotten rigging to masthead with wicker basket of orange bombs; waves; hurls four into boarders; wrecks starboard side; port side few survive. "Fidette had recaptured the ship!"

**Ch XIX (Fidette Becomes Mine):** Six boarders escape under spar. All boats destroyed. Dead bodies over side. Kantoon dead of knife (Lascar). Clark lays Kantoon in cabin bunk. Clark addresses crew; delays succession; plans civil marriage before Kantoonship. Civil marriage: bride and groom approach mainmast from opposite ends; circle three times; sprig of bay; shark-tooth necklace/pink fish-scale; "It is well; amen." Baptism with rain water. Bride kisses groom; groom kisses her pink feet. Kantoon's funeral: sewn in tarp, anchor weight, feet-first. Fidette on bowsprit with octopus.

**Ch XX (Making New Boats):** Clark becomes most miserable, love vs duty. Sargasson doctrine: outsiders lawful prey; no escapes; bottoms plugged by chains to Kantoon's cabin. Clark admits his indiscreet communication led US Bureau of Navigation to order cruisers to sink Sargasso ships. Food shortage; boats made of sea-root matting (divers cut sod holes); keel 9 ft; gum from fish scales. Root telegraph (Ceylonese idea; grapevine telegraph; Dutch-Ceylon anecdote); messages by blows on wood block; chief kantoon a day away, reply in ~2 hrs. Clark's chowder: fire at night in boiler over fo'c'sle, boatswain's fire-stick. Clark popular.

**Ch XXI (I Become a Sargasson):** Large galley *Unk-ta-hee* (60 ft, 30 paddlers) from High Priest of Sacred Fire. Clark's chronometer and quadrant. Fidette's roofless reed cabin on barge. Night journey: musicians on dulcimer-like wooden ship; needle deviates four points NW. Inland Sea (tideless). Chief Kantoon's floating palace: choir of boys, young priest; orange wine; golden dishes, gems, gold nuggets, relics.

**Ch XXII (Solemn Ceremonial):** Chinese silk robes. High Priest in black chasuble; acolytes sea-green capes; Chief's cabinet of six. Kyrie; rhapsody to sea; oath with glowing marlinspike heated in Sacred Fire; touched on right shoulder. Choir: "Blessed be the name of the Sea." Title: Clark Kantoon of Caribas. Prior commander (ex-Kantoon) must suicide per custom. Fidette weeps over leaving Happy Shark. Dance; daughters of Kantoons (40). Clark reflects on civilization.

**Ch XXIII (The New Life):** Full moon worship. Clark gets walrus-skin coat. Barge crew armed. Caribas sighted (topmast). Galley crew with tarpon scale: knife-armed boarders. Gray found tied in chair in cabin.

**Ch XXIV (Last of an Enemy):** Gray: "You never can effect your escape." Clark asks about Secor launch: Gray says he scuttled it. Barge commander: "Basta!... Let him walk with God!" Gray drowned in his chair (drowning chair = three-board easel-like seat). Clark's Baxter family board anecdote (Brooklyn). First mate retained. Blood stain on deck. Fidette settles in adjoining cabin.

**Ch XXV (Danger of an Idea):** Fidette and Donna Elenora (wife of Kantoon of Cormorant) start social reform. Clark supports. Woman suffrage (Wyoming). Mandolin song: "Wurra, wurra, wink-o-chee." Amazons club anecdote.

**Ch XXVI (The New Woman):** Clark gives captain's gig to women with homely oarsmen. Cormorant's Kantoon locks wife in sick bay. Fire tea parties; cheeks stained with ogalla juice; covetousness; bartering. Sacred Light flashes: "Sacred Flint has been stolen!" Fidette, first mate, crew suicides by drowning. Fidette: "We are lost!"

**Ch XXVII (Envy Finds a Place):** First mate: Sacred Flint stolen; thief to be burned/roasted over Sacred Fire. Fidette confesses: Elenora asked for flint; Fidette refused; Elenora borrowed flint from Chief's daughter. Clark has crew haul ballast flint; hammer sparks; 20 boats deliver flint to priest. Sacred Fire reassured. Fidette: "How much easier...to have somebody to do my thinking."

**Ch XXVIII (Plotting Treason):** Fidette's secret help; she retrieves engine parts from other ships. Clark overhauls engine; seaweed fuel (Amazon oleaginous kinds); anaconda; porpoise oil. Clark tells boatswain of plan. Smoke disguised by crushed barnacles and salt-wood (yellowish). Fore cabins for eight men each; padlocks (gross). Stokers locked in boiler room. 50 barrels salt pork, 100 barrels hard crackers found in hold. Missing sailor mystery.

**Ch XXIX (Caribas Under Steam):** Cutlasses collected; scissors-grinder (old man) grinds knives; Knife-Grinder's Song ("Too-ra-loo-ra-loo"). Men sleep in new cabins. Clark padlocks eight stokers; boatswain stokes. Clark plans to kill stokers if failure. Boilers filled with sea water. Steam rises 21, 40, 47, 50, … 75 lbs.

**Ch XXX (Farewell to the Floating Continent):** At 75 lbs, Clark tries lever; cylinder stuck; pours diluted sulphuric acid into cylinder; 85 lbs; engine runs. Cuts seaweed cables, anchor chain out. Passes Happy Shark silently. Sinks/rams Sargasson barge (30 men). Oil; 115 lbs; 15 mph. Sacred Fire message: "The Caribas is gone! Her Kantoon shall die. A Kantoonship to his captor!" Clark: "Our next address, I hope, will be New York." Two days north; fuel exhausted; staysails from blankets. Four days; German steamer *Nordland* (Gibraltar–NY); 20 men help; six days to New York, anchored at the Horseshoe. Telegram from Triplett & Jones: "Proceed Santos, then Buenos Ayres for orders." Clark: shipowners lack gratitude. END.

## BOOK 2: GIRL SCOUTS IN ARIZONA AND NEW MEXICO
Author: Lillian Elizabeth Roy. 1923, Grosset & Dunlap (George Sully & Co.). Chapters 1–17.

**Cast:** Juliet "Julie" Lee (Leader; writes for *Elmertown Record*; secretly; aspires to author; photographer); Elizabeth "Betty" Lee (twin, timid, innocent); Joan Allison (Corporal; teasing); Hester Wynant (camera, Patrol One); Ruth Bentley (to Europe); Anne Bailey (sister Eleanor's wedding late July; joins August); Amy Ward (mother Mrs. Ward relents); Judith and Edith Blake (Edie stays home; Mrs. Blake refuses); Mrs. Vernon "Verny" (Captain, founder); Mr. Vernon "Uncle Verny"; Mr. Gilroy "Gilly" (Denver; "Gilly-of-the-Dandelioners"; Adirondack estate; Rockies host); Tally (Indian guide; dialect; "Boss"; "Mees Jule"); Mary (maid); Ranger Tom Sanderson "Sandy" (Univ. of Albuquerque engineering; Cimarron Range; Panchuelo; horse Snubby); Mr. Burt (newspaperman; Bursum Bill); Ranger Johnson ("Johnny"), Oliver (Grass Mountain); Victor Adair (dark, quick) and Godfrey Chase (blond, slow); Padre Miguel (88); Mr. Balmore (Denver gentleman in Laguna); Lo (Lorenzo, Navajo guide); Mr. Walters (Gallup hotel manager); Lorenzo Hubbell ("King" of northern Arizona, Ganado); John Sweetwater (Navajo boy); Mother Superior; Phil Morton (Elmertown editor, Julie's admirer).

**Ch 1 (Plans for Southwest Trip):** Dandelion Troop. Mrs. Vernon: telegram from Gilly. Gilly's long letter: travel light; Chicago Limited from Philadelphia Sunday; meet Monday in Chicago; "flag it like Julie"; suit-cases as pillows; tents; Japanese parasols; ice near Gallinas Canyon. Tally to guide; Omney has other party. Route undecided; Enchanted Canyon swim joke. Mrs. Vernon: "I wish I was their mother." Proposal: girls join later by telegram; Joan keeps parents posted; postcards. Ends with ice-cream and layer cake.

**Ch 2 (Julie's Secret Ambition):** Train to Chicago. Gilly at station singing "Oh, say can you see." Lunch at caterer; Michigan Boulevard; Edgewater Beach tea (Lake Michigan colors). Sleeping car: Julie writes articles for *Elmertown Record* secretly. Kansas City (Mr. Vernon meets; stopover). La Junta: Tally boards. Trinidad: Cardenas hotel; elk-skin boots from Indian family near Raton (Mr. Gilroy amazed at price); moccasins; Mr. Vernon extra $10.

**Ch 3 (On the Old Santa Fé Trail):** Horse trader: nine ponies, three burros; $20–30 each per month; freight from Gallup/Flagstaff/Williams; insured via agent. Tally names: White Star (Julie's pony), Slow Poke (tent burro), Spark (stove burro), Good-for-Nuttin' (Nuttin'), Sweetie (Joan's), Stick (Tally's mule). Raton trail; Forest Ranger Sanderson meets them; Sandy's background; he rides with them. Sky-line Trail. Falls; Julie poses at leaning pine; loses footing; vines tear; faints on ledge. Tally climbs, carries her up. Mrs. Vernon's ammonia. Hester's camera: film exhausted (kept turning key). Note on stick for Ranger. Sanderson absent.

**Ch 4 (Julie Makes a Conquest):** Tally takes wrong trail, lands at lake camp (mist). Sanderson rides in at 1 AM after overtaking the trail (Snubby whinnies). Cold swim; fish; Julie flirts; Joan teases; Gilly and Vernon find trout by Ranger. Sanderson: Spanish Peaks, Fisher's Peak (named for army officer), Simpson's Rest, Las Animas River ("River of Lost Souls"), 1866 Ute fight. Sandy's duty first. Ends Springer.

**Ch 5 (Sandy Has His Say):** Springer (~1,000 people; flour/fruit). Burt meets Sandy at Springer hotel; ordered to Castañeda, Las Vegas. Tally sent by freight with burros; Sandy rides with party. Wagon Mound, Optimo, Valmora (TB sanatorium), Watrous, Mora Canyon. Reading-room debate: Sandy vs Burt on Bursum Bill (Pueblo lands; 1913 Supreme Court; Mescalero Bill for national park leaseholds; water rights). Julie privately gives Burt her notes. Joan sees.

**Ch 6 (Pecos Forests):** Las Vegas: three cities; Hot Springs; Gallinas Canyon ice (60,000 tons/yr). Pecos Forest 750,000 acres; Rangers' trails (600 miles). Bernal Creek; Pecos River camp near Blanchard; Pecos town (adobe, 8,000 ft). Ranger Johnson takes them; Apache Inn; Pecos Canyon; Grass Mountain (Johnson and Oliver). Campfire: Tally's Beaver and Porcupine legend (Julie writes it for the *Record*; porcupine's head; Ground-hog; North Wind).

**Ch 7 (Where Are the Burros?):** Oliver takes Lake Park tour; burros hobbled at Winsor. Tracks show two men driving burros down-trail. Pipe ash. Tally finds tributary; Sandy's group; Tally takes Colt; scouts split; Bishop's Lodge. Sandy hiding behind newspaper; rides to Santa Fé for guides. Gilly and Tally return at 11:45 PM with burros.

**Ch 8 (Gilly Turns Forest Ranger):** Gilly's account: smoke near Winsor/Lake Park; forest fire; Rangers Oliver and Johnson; 100,000 acres territory; fire fought with axes, mats; Ruins area; Tally's disappearance; "Ah! dat goot job done clean" (Tally). Scouts want Tally's tale.

**Ch 9 (Tally and the Rustlers):** Tally in moccasins; trampled bushes; camp fire quenched; outlaws Ben and Bill (Bill cooks; Ben tied by Tally with rope, gagged with bandanna); Bill's Colt taken; hands tied; horses (high-bred, rich New Yorkers'); Tally wakes fire; forest blaze behind them; Tally leads down; rejoins Sandy and men at Lodge. Reward $500 from New Yorkers; Tally refuses it.

**Ch 10 (Ancient Ruins and Modern Romance):** Nambe, Tesuque (pottery "gods"), Cuyamunque, Nambe Falls, Chimayo (blankets), Truchas River, Trampas, Ranchos de Taos, Taos Pueblo (seven stories; kivas). Adair and Chase join (they own the two thoroughbreds). Burt, Julie visit ruins. San Juan, Santa Cruz, Puye Ruins (1600 rooms), San Ildefonso; Santa Fé; Belnap Ranch.

**Ch 11 (Padre Miguel's Story):** Piazza at Santa Fé. Padre Miguel (88; 70 years a shepherd). Old Palace (Governor's Palace), Spanish lady's justice; Fonda and custom house; caravan (50 days); Isleta friar (warns flock; body undecayed). Bursum Bill. Mr. Vernon: rent cars for points of interest; wrote letters to other scouts' fathers. Cars hired by Sandy; Sandy, Burt, Adair, Chase.

**Ch 12 (Julie's Tête-à-Tête):** Jemez Forests; City of the Dead (Frijoles Canyon; cliff dwellings; ladders; stone circle; Painted Cave). Week of visits (Tiffany Turquoise Mine, Bonanza, Ortiz placers, Aztec ruins, Chaco Canyon). Gilly's friends delayed from Denver. Surprise: Anne, Judith, Amy arrive by train. Julie's writing revealed. Albuquerque: Alvarado Hotel; University of NM. Julie vs Sandy: "Are you thawing?" Balcony tête-à-tête; Sandy wants letters; Julie promises to think; gives address: "Glorieta"-type; "Here's my post office address—Julie, dear!"

**Ch 13 (The Enchanted Mesa):** Sandy leaves (Panchuelo). Burt goes to Gallup. Laguna by wagon (Balmore's advice). Mirage of mountain vanishing. Acoma pueblo (357 ft wall; ladders; church 40 years; walls 10 ft thick). Council: route limited to one month in Arizona; Painted Desert, Petrified Forests, Grand Cañon, Hualapai, Prescott Junction, Salt River, Gila, Apache Trail, Roosevelt Dam, Tucson, Houston, Galveston steamer to New York.

**Ch 14 (St. Michael's Mission):** Local train Laguna–Gallup; conductor (Cañon de Chelly, White House). Burt leaves for Zuñi with native guide. El Navajo hotel; Walters' advice: autos to St. Michael's; sell burros at Gallup (lease allows leaving at Gallup; fraction-of-month clause; wire to Trinidad). Tally brings horses by freight. Autos carry tents and stove. Mission: Father; Mother Superior; Navajo school; supper; John Sweetwater's "White Feather" tent-peg trick; Nature Game.

**Ch 15 (The Painted Desert):** Julie writes to Sandy (general topics only). Lorenzo (Lo) guide. Ganado trading post; Lorenzo Hubbell; mission house; Navajo dances; Navajo kids herd sheep; Lo points to San Francisco peaks. Water-pool half way to Keam's (Ream's) Canyon; sore muscles. Cold night; fire. Simoon (sandstorm); Joan's horse falls into gravel pit, she saves him; Anne inhales alkali. Ream's Canyon trader; Kit Carson monument; school. Moki villages on tufa. Julie: "beggars description." Gilly quotes Cobb. Lo refuses to go beyond Navajo Land. Adamana (petrified forest). Tally wants horses rested; Gilly insists on riding.

**Ch 16 (Region of the Petrified Forests):** Camp; Gilly's flood tale (trees, Inland lake, colored minerals). First Forest: Eagle's Head; Petrified Bridge (111 ft). Chalcedony Park; Rainbow Forest. Adamana host suggests Lava Fields, Sunset Crater, Diablo Canyon, Meteorite Mountain, Williams, Flagstaff (Lowell Observatory). Julie's Record articles (Sunset Crater; Meteorite Mountain, 200 ft mound, >1 mile bowl; Cañon Diablo). Refused: Cañon de Chelly, Betatakin/Kitsiel, Hopi villages, Walnut Canyon (visited), Montezuma's Castle (47 mi south; skipped). Telegram from Trinidad horse dealer: "Ship back freight collect." Saddle horses sent home; pack-horses sold at Williams ($30 each; Tally's account: $65 cost each at St. Michael's); profit split 50-50. "Gilly turning horse-trader!"

**Ch 17 (Bright Angel Trail):** Train from Williams; sarcastic tourist. El Tovar avoided; John Bass Camp. Sunset at Grand Cañon; Betty sobs; Gilly's sunset show. Dinner in camp. Sunrise; bacon. Descent Bright Angel trail: 23 tourists; Betty afraid (Hester and Amy stay for her; then go); burros; woman wants to go back ("Lizzie"); Julie's mule at corner (half over edge; Tally halts line); Indian Gardens; Jacob's Ladder; Devil's Corkscrew ("devil of a corkscrew," Vernon). Bottom: camp on sand. Ribbon Falls; Phantom Ranch; Hermit trail; Santa Maria Spring; Lion Canyon; Hermit Cabins; Cape Butte; Tonto trail. Photos/flora/birds (240 species, cactus, ocotillo "Devil's Claw," night-blooming cereus, phacelia, Arizona dandelion). Boxes shipped to Elmertown. Julie's book idea (Burt). Letters for Julie from Sandy (postmarked Glorieta). Gilly's telegram: lawyer; Adirondack estate title; court opens September; must return. All decide to go back with him. Tally: "Don' leaf Tally outen dat mountain climb." Chorus: "Motion made and seconded by our chairman, who is the whole thing." Julie: "So _he_ says."
